name: Cakemail
description: Cakemail is an email marketing and transactional email platform for managing audiences, campaigns, senders, forms, templates, reports, and email delivery through its REST API.

authentication.name: Bearer Token
authentication.description: Cakemail API access token used as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

setupGuide.title: Create or provide a Cakemail access token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Cakemail API tokens are sensitive server-side credentials. Use an active access token from the Cakemail token endpoint or a token supplied by your administrator.

steps.title: Open Cakemail developer authentication docs
steps.description: Review the Cakemail API getting started guide for the token endpoint and supported bearer-token flow.

steps.title: Generate or retrieve an access token
steps.description: Create a token through the Cakemail API token endpoint or retrieve the access token your administrator prepared for this connection.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud Cakemail connection form and paste the access token into the API key field.

name: Campaign Monitor

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Connect Campaign Monitor with OAuth 2.0.

setupGuide.title: How to connect Campaign Monitor
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: An app owner must register a Campaign Monitor OAuth application and configure its Client ID and Client Secret on this MindCloud app before end-user connections can complete. When Campaign Monitor asks for a redirect URI, use the callback URL shown by MindCloud during connection setup.

steps.title: Sign in to Campaign Monitor
steps.description: Sign in to the Campaign Monitor account that owns the clients, lists, campaigns, and templates you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Register an OAuth application
steps.description: In Campaign Monitor, open Integrations from the top navigation, then choose OAuth Registration in the right sidebar. Register a new OAuth application and keep the generated Client ID and Client Secret.

steps.title: Configure the MindCloud app
steps.description: Have a MindCloud app owner add the Campaign Monitor Client ID and Client Secret to this app configuration before any end-user tries to connect.

steps.title: Approve access
steps.description: Once the app owner has configured the client credentials, start the Campaign Monitor connection in MindCloud, review the requested permissions, and approve the connection.

setupGuide.title: Find your Campaign Monitor API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Campaign Monitor account settings for the account you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Open Campaign Monitor account settings
steps.description: Sign in to Campaign Monitor and open your account settings page.

steps.title: Copy the API key you want MindCloud to use
steps.description: From the API keys area, copy the key for the account you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the copied value into the Basic authentication API key field for this Campaign Monitor connection.

name: Castor EDC
description: Access Castor EDC studies, users, participants, records, forms, and clinical data through the official Castor EDC API.

authentication.name: OAuth2 client credentials
authentication.description: OAuth2 client-credentials authentication for the Castor EDC API.
authentication.notes: These credentials are valid against the US Castor region. The draft app is pinned to https://us.castoredc.com for both token exchange and API requests. Castor documents that the default scope grants access to all endpoints, and this credential path succeeds with the default scope. Before changing regions, verify the target study host because Castor client credentials are region-specific.

setupGuide.title: Connect Castor EDC
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an active Castor account, access to the correct Castor server region for your study, and the right study permissions before the API credentials will return useful data.

steps.title: Sign in to Castor CDMS
steps.description: Open the Castor CDMS environment that matches your study region and sign in with the account that owns the study access you want to use for the API.

steps.title: Open the Castor EDC API credentials page
steps.description: From the blue bar, open Account, choose Settings, then open the Castor EDC API subtab.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials
steps.description: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the MindCloud connection form. If you regenerate the secret, replace the old value everywhere because older secrets stop working.

steps.title: Confirm the server region
steps.description: Make sure the draft app is pointed at the same Castor region as the study you want to access. Castor publishes separate API hosts for EU, UK, US, and AU environments.

actions.name: Create Patient
actions.description: Creates a new patient in Cerbo.

arguments.name: Inactive
arguments.description: Sets the patient status. Accepts the following values: | Value | Result | |---|---| | `"prospective"` or `"-1"` | Prospective patient | | `"0"`, empty, or omitted | Active patient (default) | | `"inactive"` or `"1"` | Inactive patient | | `"deceased"` or `"dead"` or `"2"` | Deceased patient | **Important — GET response behavior:** When reading patient data via GET, the `inactive` field is cast to a boolean rather than returning the original value. This means: | Stored status | `inactive` in GET | `patient_status_description` in GET | |---|---|---| | Prospective (`-1`) | `true` | `"prospective"` | | Active (`0`) | `false` | `"active"` | | Inactive (`1`) | `true` | `"inactive"` | | Deceased (`2`) | `true` | `"deceased"` | Because `inactive` returns `true` for prospective, inactive, and deceased patients alike, you **must** use the `patient_status_description` field to determine the actual status. This is a known legacy serialization issue where the create/update and read representations differ.

name: Cerebras AI
description: Cerebras AI provides high-performance inference APIs for chat completions, text completions, model discovery, public model metadata, batch jobs, file management, metrics, and preview management operations.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate Cerebras inference API requests with a Cerebras API key sent as an Authorization bearer token.
authentication.notes:
Create an API key in Cerebras Cloud and paste the raw key value. Cerebras standard inference endpoints use `Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>`. Management preview endpoints documented under `/management/v1/...` require a separate management API key and an `org_name`; do not reuse the standard inference key for those routes.

Suggested setup:
1. Go to Cerebras Cloud and create an API key.
2. Store the raw key value as this app connection.
3. Use standard inference routes under `https://api.cerebras.ai/v1/...` with that key.
4. Use separate credentials only if you need management preview endpoints.

name: ChartMogul
description: Track subscription revenue, customers, and retention metrics

authentication.name: API Key (Basic Auth)
authentication.description: Use your ChartMogul API key as the username. Use the same API key as the password.

setupGuide.title: Connect ChartMogul with an API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a ChartMogul API key from your own account.

steps.title: Open your ChartMogul profile settings
steps.description: Sign in to ChartMogul, open Profile > View Profile, and choose API Keys in the sidebar.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.description: Click ADD API KEY and create a key for this MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the new API key and keep it available while you finish the MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Enter the key in MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud credential form, paste the API key into Username.

steps.title: Use the same key as Password
steps.description: ChartMogul allows the Basic Auth password to be blank or the same as the API key. For MindCloud, paste the same API key into Password so the request builder sends valid Basic Auth headers.

name: Chaser
description: Chaser manages Slack-scoped task lists for the connected workspace, exposing task retrieval and later task CRUD/command workflows through the Chaser task API.

authentication.name: Bearer Token
authentication.description: Use the Chaser webhook token as the bearer token for Chaser API and webhook requests.

setupGuide.title: Get your Chaser bearer token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Appsmindcloud Slack workspace and the /chaser slash command.

steps.title: Open the Appsmindcloud Slack workspace
steps.description: Open the workspace where Chaser is installed and confirm you can access the target channel toda-a-empresa-slack.

steps.title: Run the Chaser token command
steps.description: In Slack, run `/chaser get-chaser-webhook-token` from any channel where the command is available.

steps.title: Paste the token into the connection
steps.description: Copy the returned token value and paste it into the `API Key` field for this connection. Chaser expects it as a bearer token and the app will send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` automatically.

steps.title: Verify workspace context
steps.description: Use workspace `appsmindcloud` (`T0AP5JGGB7S`), channel `toda-a-empresa-slack` (`C0AP5JGLUCQ`), and user `U0AMVSLQWG7` when validating tenant-specific behavior.

actions.name: Create Task
actions.description: Creates a new task in Chaser.

arguments.name: Assignee
arguments.description: Assignee email address or Slack user group handle. Multiple assignees can be comma-separated.

arguments.name: Due Time
arguments.description: Optional due time in HH:mm format using the task creator timezone.

arguments.name: Channel
arguments.description: Optional Slack channel name. Omit to create the task in the creator's direct-message context.

arguments.name: Multi-Assign Strategy
arguments.description: Optional strategy for multiple assignees: volunteer or round_robin.

steps.title: Copy your API key

name: ChatBotKit

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Use that API secret key as the ChatBotKit connection value in MindCloud.

name: Checkmob
description: Checkmob verified draft: 63 actions are now in QA with live evidence across auth, client read/create/update flows, bulk client creation, client addresses, client notes, people create/get/update/delete flows, person-to-client linking, segment create/get/update/delete and link/unlink flows, checklist link/unlink flows, group update, service-order create/get/status-change/delete flows, and the supporting lookup/list families. The draft inventory totals 71 actions: 67 official Swagger-backed operations, one retained semantic duplicate search action, and three older candidate detail routes that are not present in Swagger and return HTTP 404. Eight actions remain blocked with explicit notes: Create Group (provider returns HTTP 500 even for Swagger-shaped payloads), Get/Update Person Address (tenant lacks a person record with an existing address row), Get/Update Service (tenant currently has zero service records), and the candidate Get Service Status by ID, Get Step by ID, and Get Temperature by ID routes that return HTTP 404.

actions.name: Create Checkout Page
actions.description: Creates a checkout page in Checkout Page.

arguments.name: Name
arguments.description: Internal page name used in your dashboard and API responses.

arguments.name: Slug
arguments.description: Page URL slug. For events and forms the slug defaults to the slugified version of your `title`. For checkouts the slug defaults to the slugified version of your `productData.title`.

arguments.name: Status
arguments.description: Initial publication status. Defaults to "published" if not provided.

arguments.name: Product Data
arguments.description:
Product configuration for checkout pages.

Use this object to define pricing mode, subscription/payment plan behavior, inventory, variants, and conditional variant visibility.

Common setup patterns:
- Standard one-time checkout: set `price.amount`, `price.currency`, and keep `price.pricingType` as `single`.
- Variant-driven pricing: set `price.pricingType` to `multiple`, then define `variants` and per-option `additionalChargeAmount`.
- Subscriptions (recurring): configure `price.recurring`.
- Payment plans (fixed installments): configure `price.paymentPlan` with `planIterations`.

Important rules:
- You cannot set both `price.recurring` and `price.paymentPlan`.
- `price.payWhatYouWant` cannot be used with subscriptions or payment plans.
- `trialPeriodDays` and `startDate` are mutually exclusive within `recurring` and `paymentPlan`.
- For conditional variant logic (`showHideLogic`) or `preselect`, set a `key` on variants/options to enable cross-references. Keys are not persisted.

arguments.name: Fields
arguments.description: Custom checkout fields to create. If one of your fields must be an `email` element and `required` must be true. Defaults to a name and email field if none are set.

arguments.name: Customize Checkout Confirmation
arguments.description: If set to true `confirmationCheckoutMessage` and `confirmationCheckoutTitle` will be displayed on the confirmation page. Defaults to `false`.

arguments.name: Allow Dynamic Title
arguments.description: Allow page title to be overridden via URL query parameters.

arguments.name: Allow Dynamic Description
arguments.description: Allow page description to be overridden via URL query parameters.

arguments.name: Close Popup On Click Outside
arguments.description: Whether a popup embed closes when clicking outside the container. Defaults to `false`.

arguments.name: Redirect
arguments.description: If enabled, redirects the customer to the specified URL before the page loads.

arguments.name: After Payment Action
arguments.description: Behavior after checkout. `confirmation` shows the confirmation page. `checkout` redirects to `redirectPageId`. `redirect` sends the customer to `redirectUrl`. Defaults to `confirmation`.

arguments.description: A positive integer representing the amount to subtract from an invoice total (required if `percentOff` is not passed).

arguments.name: Currency
arguments.description: Three-letter ISO code for the currency of the amountOff parameter (required if `amountOff` is passed).

arguments.name: Duration In Months
arguments.description: A positive integer representing the number of months the coupon applies for (required if `duration === repeating`)

arguments.description: A positive float larger than 0, and smaller or equal to 100, that represents the discount the coupon will apply (required if `amountOff` is not passed).

arguments.name: Applies To Setup Fee

arguments.name: Page Ids

arguments.name: Ticket Type Ids
arguments.description: List of ticket type IDs that this coupon can be used with. Ticket ticket ids must belong to a page specified in the `pageIds` array.

arguments.name: Max Redemptions
arguments.description: The total amount of times this coupon can be used. Doesn't limit a single customer from redeeming multiple times.

arguments.name: Redeem By
arguments.description: The ISO datetime that this coupon must be used before.

Cisco Umbrella
description: Cisco Umbrella is Cisco's cloud security platform for managing users, deployments, policies, threat investigation, and security reporting through the Cisco Umbrella API.

authentication.name: API Key Connection
authentication.description: Cisco Umbrella API key connection. The API key and key secret are exchanged with Cisco's OAuth2 client-credentials token endpoint before API calls.
authentication.notes:
Connection setup:

1. In Cisco Umbrella, create an API key with the scopes needed for the actions you plan to use.
2. Copy the API key and key secret.
3. In MindCloud, enter the API key as the OAuth client ID and the key secret as the OAuth client secret.
4. This is an API key connection in Cisco terminology, implemented as OAuth2 client credentials because Cisco issues short-lived bearer tokens from https://api.umbrella.com/auth/v2/token.
5. Use read scopes for admin, deployments, investigate, policies, and reports; add write scopes only for write actions such as adding destinations to a destination list.
authentication.scopes: admin.users:read admin.roles:read admin.organizations:read deployments.networks:read deployments.sites:read deployments.internalnetworks:read deployments.roamingcomputers:read policies.destinationLists:read policies.destinations:read policies.destinations:write investigate.investigate:read investigate.bulk:read reports.aggregations:read reports.appDiscovery:read reports.apiusage:read

steps.description: In Clappia, open Workplace Settings, go to the Preferences tab, then open API Keys. Generate an API key if you do not already have one, and copy it to a secure place.

steps.title: Find your workplace ID
steps.description: In Workplace Settings, open the general workplace information panel and copy the Workplace ID for the same workplace as the API key.

steps.title: Enter both values in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the API key into the API Key field and the Workplace ID into the Workplace ID field when creating the connection.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Clarifai account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Clarifai account, your user ID, and a personal access token (PAT).

steps.title: Sign in to Clarifai
steps.description: Open the Clarifai login page and sign in to the account you want to connect.

steps.title: Copy your user ID
steps.description: In Clarifai, open Settings and choose Account. Locate your user ID and copy it.

steps.title: Copy or create a PAT
steps.description: Open Settings and choose Secrets. Copy an existing Personal Access Token, or create a new one if needed.

steps.title: Paste both values into MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form, paste the PAT into API Key and paste the user ID into User ID.

setupGuide.title: Connect ClassMarker API

steps.title: Choose what this key can access

steps.title: Save the key and copy both values
steps.description: When you save, ClassMarker generates an API key and its matching API secret. Copy both values now and paste them into the MindCloud connection form as API Key and API Secret.

name: Coast
description: Use the Coast API to manage account settings, cards, departments, locations, people, policies, roles, purchases, and vehicles within a Coast account.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Coast API key from the Coast portal to authenticate requests.

setupGuide.title: Connect Coast with an API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need admin access to your Coast portal so you can generate a new API key for this connection.

steps.title: Open the API keys page in Coast
steps.description: Sign in to your Coast portal, open Integrations, then go to the API keys page.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Click New API Key, enter a name for this integration, and finish the key creation flow.

steps.title: Copy the API key into the connection form
steps.description: Copy the newly created API key and paste it into the API Key field in the connection form. Keep the key secure because Coast only authenticates requests with this value.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.notes: CoinCap API 3.0 uses bearer authentication on the documented REST surface at rest.coincap.io/v3. Provide your CoinCap Pro API key and the app will send it as an Authorization bearer token.

setupGuide.title: Connect CoinCap
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a CoinCap API key from your CoinCap Pro account.

steps.title: Open CoinCap API 3.0 docs
steps.description: Open the official CoinCap API 3.0 documentation and confirm you are using the Pro REST API.

steps.title: Copy your CoinCap API key
steps.description: From your CoinCap Pro account, copy the API key you want this app to use.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and paste the API key into the CoinCap connection when prompted.

name: CoinGate
description: Accept cryptocurrency payments, manage refunds and billing, run payouts, and inspect ledger activity in CoinGate.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Connect CoinGate with a merchant access token generated from the CoinGate dashboard.

setupGuide.title: Create a CoinGate API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the CoinGate merchant dashboard for the account you want to connect. If you plan to test in sandbox, generate a separate token at sandbox.coingate.com because live and sandbox tokens are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Sign in to CoinGate
steps.description: Log in with the merchant account you want to connect.

steps.title: Open API Management
steps.description: In the left navigation, go to Integrations, then Merchant Tools, then open API Management.

steps.title: Create a new API credential
steps.description: Use the add button in the top-right corner, complete the form, and save the new credential.

steps.title: Copy the access token
steps.description: Copy the generated access token immediately because CoinGate only shows it once.

name: Comm100
description: Comm100 is an AI-powered omnichannel customer service platform for live chat, ticketing, messaging, knowledge base, voice, and customer support operations.

authentication.name: API Key (Basic Auth)
authentication.description: Authenticate with the Comm100 agent email as the username and the Comm100 API key as the password. Comm100 also requires siteId on API requests when using API-key authentication.
authentication.notes: Comm100 API-key authentication uses HTTP Basic Auth. Use the agent email as the username, the Comm100 API key as the password, and provide the Comm100 siteId for API requests.

credentials.name: Site ID
credentials.description: Comm100 site ID required on API requests when using API-key authentication.

setupGuide.title: Connect Comm100 with API Key Authentication
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Comm100 agent login, that agent's API key, and the Comm100 site ID for the target workspace.

steps.title: Sign in to the Comm100 Control Panel
steps.description: Open your Comm100 Control Panel and sign in with the agent account you want MindCloud to use for API access.

steps.title: Copy the agent email and API key
steps.description: In the bottom-left navigation area, open the avatar menu and click the agent name. In the My Profile drawer, expand More Information and copy the login email and API key for this agent.

steps.title: Copy the Comm100 site ID
steps.description: In the Comm100 Control Panel, go to Global Settings > Site Profile and copy the Site ID from that page.

steps.title: Enter the connection values in MindCloud
steps.description: When creating or updating the MindCloud test connection, enter the agent email as the username, the Comm100 API key as the password, and the Site ID in the Site ID field.

steps.title: Run the test connection
steps.description: Use the MindCloud connection test after saving the credentials. Comm100 API-key authentication requires both Basic Auth credentials and siteId on API requests.

name: Communi App
description: CommuniApp is a community platform for managing events, announcements, recommendations, offers, quests, polls, messaging, groups, and donations.

authentication.name: API Token
authentication.description: Use the CommuniApp REST API access token from Admin -> Integration -> REST-API. The token is sent in the X-Authorization header with the required Bearer prefix.

setupGuide.title: Connect CommuniApp REST API
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need admin access to a CommuniApp tenant and the tenant URL for the community you want to connect.

steps.title: Open your CommuniApp admin area
steps.description: Sign in to the admin area of the CommuniApp tenant you want to connect.

steps.title: Open the REST API settings
steps.description: In the admin area, open Integration and then REST-API. The official API docs describe this location as Admin-Bereich -> Integration -> REST-API and reference route /page/integration/tab/rest.

steps.title: Copy the access token
steps.description: Copy the Zugangstoken exactly as shown in the REST-API page.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the copied token into the API key field when creating the MindCloud connection. Do not add a second Bearer prefix in the credential field; the app adds the required header format automatically.

steps.title: Keep the main group ID and app ID handy
steps.description: Copy the Haupt-Gruppen-ID and App-ID from the same REST-API page. You will use the main group ID in many collection actions, such as listing events for a group.

steps.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 (3LO)

steps.title: Copy your client credentials
steps.description: Open Settings and copy the Client ID and Secret for the app so you can enter them when creating the connection.

steps.title: Reconnect after scope changes

actions.name: Get Job
actions.description: Retrieve a single job information by its unique ID

actions.name: Get Timesheet Totals
actions.description: Retrieves detailed work records for each employee within a specified date range. This endpoint is designed to support payroll processing by providing total worked hours, categorized by pay rules and resource (if applied in the account settings). Ideal for integrating with external payroll systems to ensure accurate information. The pay rate will be presented in case it is defined within the account. If an automated unpaid break is applied, it will  be deducted from the total hours value. In order to retrieve approved paid time-off (PTO) and manual break information, please use the Get time activities endpoint. Hours will be presented in decimal format. The time period is limited to 45 days.

name: ConnectPay
description: ConnectPay banking APIs for BaaS clients, accounts, payments, cards, merchant payments, and related payment operations.

authentication.name: OAuth access token
authentication.description: ConnectPay API requests use an OAuth Bearer access token generated from the ConnectPay authCode/token flow. Paste a valid access token into the API key field for this connection.

setupGuide.title: Create a ConnectPay access token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a ConnectPay DevApp, an online banking user authorized for the target customer, and the required ConnectPay API products enabled on the DevApp.

steps.title: Confirm the DevApp configuration
steps.description: In the ConnectPay Developer Portal, use the ConnectPay DevApp with the registered redirect URI and required API products.

steps.title: Generate an authCode
steps.description: In ConnectPay Online Banking, generate an authCode for the customer and grants you need. The code is valid for 24 hours.

steps.title: Exchange the authCode for tokens
steps.description: Call ConnectPay's Generate Access Token API with HTTP Basic authentication using the DevApp Client ID and Client Secret, then copy the returned access_token.

steps.title: Create the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Paste the access_token into the API key field. MindCloud sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

actions.name: Add Image Watermark to PDF
actions.description: Adds an image watermark to a PDF with ConvertAPI.

arguments.name: File
arguments.description: File to be converted. Value can be URL or file content.

arguments.name: File Name
arguments.description: The `FileName` property defines the name of the output file(s) generated by the file conversion API, ensuring safe and unique file naming. It sanitizes input filenames to remove potentially harmful characters, automatically appends the correct file extension based on the target format, and includes an indexing feature to distinguish multiple output files from a single input. For example, converting `report.docx` to PDF format might result in `report.pdf` for a single file, or `report_0.pdf`, `report_1.pdf` for multiple files, ensuring each output file is uniquely identifiable.

arguments.name: Page Box

actions.name: Compare DOCX Files
actions.description: Compares DOCX files and highlights differences in ConvertAPI.

arguments.name: File
arguments.description: File to be converted. Value can be URL or file content.

arguments.name: Compare File
arguments.description: Specifies the Word document with which the specified document is compared.

arguments.name: File Name
arguments.description: The `FileName` property defines the name of the output file(s) generated by the file conversion API, ensuring safe and unique file naming. It sanitizes input filenames to remove potentially harmful characters, automatically appends the correct file extension based on the target format, and includes an indexing feature to distinguish multiple output files from a single input. For example, converting `report.docx` to PDF format might result in `report.pdf` for a single file, or `report_0.pdf`, `report_1.pdf` for multiple files, ensuring each output file is uniquely identifiable.

arguments.name: Password
arguments.description: Sets the password to open protected documents.

arguments.name: Compare Level
arguments.description: The property defines the granularity of comparisons between documents or text segments. It determines the precision of the comparison process, allowing users to specify whether differences are identified based on larger text blocks, such as words or sentences, or at a more detailed level, such as characters or formatting.

arguments.name: Compare Formatting
arguments.description: Determines whether to indicate variations in formatting between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Case Changes
arguments.description: Determines whether to highlight discrepancies in capitalization between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Whitespace
arguments.description: Determines whether to identify dissimilarities in whitespace, such as gaps or paragraphs, between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Tables
arguments.description: Determines whether to evaluate variations in the information presented within tables between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Headers
arguments.description: Determines whether to contrast divergences in headers and footers between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Footnotes
arguments.description: Determines whether to compare differences in footnotes and endnotes between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Textboxes
arguments.description: Determines whether to assess differences in the information presented within text boxes between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Fields
arguments.description: Determines whether to detect disparities in fields between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Comments
arguments.description: Determines whether to evaluate distinctions in comments between the two documents.

arguments.name: Compare Moves
arguments.description: Indicates the name of the individual to credit for modifications when comparing the two documents.

arguments.name: Accept Revisions
arguments.description: Specifies whether to accept revisions before document comparison.

arguments.description: Specifies whether to remove the base fonts from the PDF file.

arguments.name: Subset Embedded Fonts
arguments.description: Output PDF should only contain font characters utilized in the original document, and any unused glyphs from all fonts in the document should be removed.

arguments.name: Remove Forms
arguments.description: Remove PDF forms from the PDF file.

arguments.name: Remove Duplicates
arguments.description: Remove duplicate fonts and color profiles from the PDF file.

arguments.name: Optimize
arguments.description: Optimize page content streams in the PDF file.

arguments.name: Remove Piece Information
arguments.description: Remove piece information dictionaries like Adobe Illustrator or Photoshop private data.

arguments.name: Remove Embedded Files
arguments.description: Remove embedded/attachments files from the PDF file.

arguments.name: Remove Structure Information
arguments.description: Remove all structure information from the PDF document.

arguments.name: Remove Metadata
arguments.description: Detach the XMP metadata embedded in the document from its catalog, clear all properties in all schemas, and remove metadata from marked content.

arguments.name: Remove Unused Resources
arguments.description: Remove references to resources such as fonts, images, patterns.

arguments.name: Linearize
arguments.description: Linearize PDF file and optimize for fast Web View.

arguments.name: Preserve PDF/A
arguments.description: Preserve the PDF/A standard in the PDF file.

arguments.name: File

For example, converting `report.docx` to PDF format might result in `report.pdf` for a single file, or `report_0.pdf`, `report_1.pdf` for multiple files, ensuring each output file is uniquely identifiable.

arguments.name: Password
arguments.description: Sets the password to open protected documents.

arguments.name: OCR Mode
arguments.description: The `OcrMode` setting controls how OCR is applied to PDF pages. In `Auto` mode, pages that already contain text are skipped, so OCR runs only where needed. In `Always` mode, OCR is applied to every page, keeping existing text while adding recognition for images and other visual content. In `Reprocess` mode, OCR is performed on the whole page, producing a fresh text layer regardless of what was there before.

arguments.name: OCR Language
arguments.description: Set the OCR language. Ask support to add your language if missing.

arguments.name: Output Type
arguments.description: This property is used to determine how the OCR layer should be returned. If the output type is PDF, the OCR layer will be embedded into the PDF file. Alternatively, if a text output is selected, the OCR layer will be returned as a text file.

arguments.name: Page Segmentation Mode
arguments.description: The **PageSegmentationMode** parameter specifies how the OCR engine segments and interprets text within PDF documents. Choosing the appropriate mode enhances OCR accuracy by aligning closely with your document's layout and structure. Select one of the available modes to control text detection and layout analysis: - **SparseText** - Detects as much text as possible without enforcing any specific order. Suitable for documents containing scattered or fragmented text. - **SparseTextOsd** - Similar to SparseText, but also includes orientation and script detection (OSD). Useful for documents with rotated text or multiple scripts and languages. - **Auto** - Automatically selects the best segmentation mode based on document content. Ideal for general documents with mixed or unknown layouts. - **AutoOsd** - Combines automatic segmentation with orientation and script detection. Recommended for documents with uncertain text orientation or multilingual content. - **SingleColumn** - Assumes a single column of text with varying text sizes. Best suited for straightforward layouts. - **SingleLine** - Treats the entire image as a single line of text. Useful for single-line labels, banners, or narrow text snippets. - **SingleWord** - Treats the entire image as a single word. Ideal for recognizing isolated words or short phrases.

When the `StoreFile` parameter is set to `True`, your converted file is written to ConvertAPI’s encrypted, temporary storage and made available via a time-limited secure download URL, valid for up to 3 hours. After this period, the file is permanently deleted.
When `StoreFile` is set to `False`, conversion happens entirely in-memory. The raw file bytes are streamed back in the API response without touching disk or external storage, ensuring maximum security and zero persistence so that only you can access the content.

actions.name: Split PDF
actions.description: Splits a PDF into separate files in ConvertAPI.

arguments.name: File
arguments.description: File to be converted. Value can be URL or file content.

arguments.name: File Name
arguments.description: The `FileName` property defines the name of the output file(s) generated by the file conversion API, ensuring safe and unique file naming. It sanitizes input filenames to remove potentially harmful characters, automatically appends the correct file extension based on the target format, and includes an indexing feature to distinguish multiple output files from a single input. For example, converting `report.docx` to PDF format might result in `report.pdf` for a single file, or `report_0.pdf`, `report_1.pdf` for multiple files, ensuring each output file is uniquely identifiable.

arguments.name: Password
arguments.description: Sets the password to open protected documents.

arguments.name: Split By Pattern
arguments.description: A comma-separated sequence of positive integers defining the size of each split segment. The PDF will be divided into consecutive chunks whose page counts follow the given pattern, repeating it until all pages are consumed. For a 10-page PDF with `SplitByPattern = 3,2`, the output will be four documents containing pages `[1-3]`, `[4-5]`, `[6-8]`, and `[9-10]` (pattern repeats: 3,2,3,2).

arguments.name: Split By Range
arguments.description: Specify exactly which pages to extract by listing single pages or inclusive ranges. The API will emit one PDF per entry, in the order given. For a 10-page file with `SplitByRange = 1-3,5,7-9`, you receive three PDFs containing pages `[1–3]`, `[5]`, and `[7–9]`.

arguments.name: Split By Text Pattern
arguments.description: Splits the PDF into separate output files by starting a new document at each page whose text matches the specified regular expression. With `SplitByTextPattern = Chapter\s+\d+`, the PDF will be split at every page where “Chapter 1”, “Chapter 2”, etc., appear. If “Chapter 1” is on page 1, “Chapter 2” on page 10, and “Chapter 3” on page 20 of a 25-page PDF, you’ll get four files containing pages `[1–9]`, `[10–19]`, `[20–25]`, and any pages after the last match (if present).

arguments.name: Split By Bookmark
arguments.description: Automatically splits a source PDF into individual documents, creating a new file at every bookmarked page. When nested bookmarks are present, splitting occurs at the deepest (child) level, and each output file is named to reflect the full bookmark hierarchy - for example: `ParentBookmark-ChildBookmark.pdf`. When the source PDF has no bookmarks, the original document is returned unchanged as `no-bookmarks.pdf`.

arguments.name: Extract Pages
arguments.description: Specify a comma-separated list of pages or inclusive ranges `ExtractPages = 1,3-5,7` to pull out from the source PDF. The API will emit one PDF per entry, each containing exactly the pages defined.

arguments.name: Merge Output
arguments.description: When set to `true`, all split output files (whether defined by page ranges, custom ranges, or text-pattern segments) will be merged into a single PDF. By default `false`, the API returns one PDF per specified range.

name: Countly
description: Countly is a product analytics and customer experience platform for querying apps, users, events, dashboards, funnels, campaigns, and operational analytics through its REST API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Countly user API key. Countly REST endpoints expect the key as the api_key query parameter.
authentication.notes: Countly REST endpoints use the platform-managed API key credential as the `api_key` query parameter. Do not paste the secret into action arguments; it is injected from `credentials.apiKey`.

setupGuide.title: Connect Countly
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use a Countly user API key with permission to access the apps you want to query.

steps.title: Get your Countly API key
steps.description: Countly documents the /api-key endpoint as the way to retrieve a user's API_KEY from login credentials with Basic Authentication.

steps.title: Enter the API key
steps.description: Paste the Countly user API_KEY into the API Key field for this connection.

name: Customer.io
description: Create journeys, send messages, sync data, and analyze campaign performance.

setupGuide.title: Create a Customer.io App API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need to be an Account Admin or have the account-level permission to manage API credentials. Use an App API key for this connection, not a Track API key.

steps.title: Open API credentials in Customer.io
steps.description: Sign in to Customer.io and go to Account Settings > API Credentials.

steps.title: Create a new set of credentials for the correct workspace
steps.description: Add a new set of credentials, give it a name, and select the Customer.io workspace that MindCloud should access.

steps.title: Copy the App API key
steps.description: From the new credential set, copy the App API key and store it securely. Customer.io only shows App API keys once because they are stored as hashed values afterward.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud Customer.io connection form and paste the copied App API key into the API key field.

name: Cypress

setupGuide.title: Connect Cypress
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Cypress Cloud organization API key with access to the Enterprise Reporting Data Extract API.

steps.title: Sign in to Cypress Cloud
steps.description: Open Cypress Cloud and sign in to the organization that owns the reporting API key.

steps.title: Open the Data Extract API key location
steps.description: Navigate to the Cypress location where your organization API key for Enterprise Reporting is shown or can be generated.

steps.title: Copy the organization API key
steps.description: Copy the API key exactly as shown by Cypress.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Use the API Key field in the MindCloud connection form and save the connection.
